subject.title: Gateway crash-loops with default Node heap (~4 GB) — make 'openclaw daemon install' set NODE_OPTIONS or accept a --heap-mb flag

question: Should OpenClaw resolve this issue by landing the fixed 8192 MB generated-service default in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96250, require a tunable heap surface first, or switch to a Node CLI-argument implementation?
rationale: The bug is severe, but the permanent fix changes daemon startup defaults and intersects the repository's security policy around `NODE_OPTIONS`, which is a maintainer product and compatibility choice.

options.title: Land the fixed default
options.body: Accept the current active PR as the emergency mitigation and track a durable tuning surface separately if needed.

options.title: Require a tuning surface
options.body: Pause the active PR until maintainers choose and prove a config or CLI flag for low-memory and fleet-managed hosts.

options.title: Prefer CLI argv
options.body: Revive or fold in the CLI-argument shape so the heap cap avoids generated `NODE_OPTIONS` entirely.

recommendation.title: Land the fixed default
recommendation.body: Accept the current active PR as the emergency mitigation and track a durable tuning surface separately if needed.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest remote history across daemon service environment, wrapper, and install-planning code touched by the candidate fixes.
